intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters and equipment rentals on-site. An educational visitor center teaches about the reef ecosystem before you enter.

experiences.name: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau
experiences.description: Immerse your family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, and a feast of kalua pig, poi, and tropical dishes. This award-winning luau is set on the oceanfront and offers a genuine cultural experience suitable for all ages.

experiences.name: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout
experiences.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails through lush valleys and dramatic red-rock formations. Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The lookout points are easily accessible even for younger children.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Waikiki's gentle, rolling waves make it the world's best spot to learn to surf. Group family surf lessons with certified instructors are fun, safe, and beginner-friendly. Most families are standing on their boards within the first lesson, creating unforgettable memories on one of the most iconic beaches in the world.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional canoe rides. The evening show features a spectacular Broadway-style performance with stunning costumes and storytelling.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The lookout points are easily accessible even for younger children.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Collect baggage, arrange ground transportation (TheBus or shared shuttle to save money), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack from a nearby convenience store or hotel vending machine before resting.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport food court
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: 7-Eleven or ABC Store near the resort for a quick, affordable late-night snack (musubi, chips, drinks) — budget ~$10

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle or use TheBus Route 20 from the airport to save on transportation costs. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance since arrival is late. Pack light snacks in your carry-on for the arrival night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, head to the hotel's beachfront for a relaxing morning swim and beach walk. Explore the shoreline, collect shells, and enjoy the warm Hawaiian water — completely free!
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local beach park (such as Ala Moana Beach Park if on Oahu) for family fun. Rent a bodyboard from a local surf shop (~$10–$15/day) and enjoy the gentle waves. Kids and adults alike will love the calm lagoon-style waters perfect for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade at sunset. Watch the famous Hawaiian sunset from the shore. Head to a nearby food truck park or plate lunch spot for an affordable local dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab fresh fruit and pastries from a local farmers market or ABC Store (~$8–$12 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or grab a plate lunch from a local deli — Spam musubi, macaroni salad, and rice plate (~$10–$12)
meals.dinner: Local food truck or plate lunch restaurant — try loco moco or teriyaki chicken plate (~$12–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day after travel. Stay close to the hotel, hydrate well, and apply sunscreen generously. Ala Moana Beach Park has free parking and restroom facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument for a family-friendly hike. The trail is 1.6 miles round trip with stunning panoramic views of Honolulu and the Pacific Ocean. Entry fee is $5 per person (or $10 per vehicle). Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for an afternoon of swimming, snorkeling, and sandcastle building. Rent snorkel gear from a budget shop (~$15) and explore the colorful reef fish close to shore. The beach is free and family-friendly with lifeguards on duty.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show at Kuhio Beach Park (held Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings). Watch traditional Hawaiian hula dancing and fire knife performances — no cost to attend!

meals.breakfast: Grab acai bowls or smoothies from a local cafe (~$10–$12) before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or grab shave ice and a hot dog from a Waikiki beach vendor (~$8–$10)
meals.dinner: Ramen or poke bowl from a casual local restaurant in Waikiki (~$14–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Diamond Head entry in advance online at hawaii.goingtopark.com as timed entry reservations are required. Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and snacks for the hike. Wear comfortable closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for world-class snorkeling in a protected marine sanctuary. Entry is $25 per adult (children 12 and under free). Reservations required — book online in advance. Arrive early as spots fill up fast. See sea turtles, tropical fish, and coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Windward Coast (rent a car for the day, ~$50–$70 from a budget rental agency). Stop at Lanikai Beach — consistently rated one of the world's best beaches — for swimming and photos. Walk the Pillbox Hike for panoramic views (free, ~1 hour round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the charming town of Kailua for dinner and a stroll. Browse local boutiques and enjoy the relaxed small-town Hawaiian vibe before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery — a Hawaii institution (~$1.25 each)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Lanikai Beach — pack sandwiches, fruit, and drinks from a grocery store (~$8–$10 per person)
meals.dinner: Kailua town casual restaurant or food truck — try fish tacos or a local burger (~$12–$16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations must be made 2 days in advance at hanaumabaystatepark.com. No sunscreen with oxybenzone or octinoxate is allowed (reef-safe only). Renting a car today maximizes efficiency along the Windward Coast.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center in Laie (budget tip: purchase tickets in advance online for discounts, ~$60–$80 per adult, children discounted). Explore six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Interactive and very family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch canoe pageants on the lagoon, try traditional games, and participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and weaving.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Ha: Breath of Life evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center (included in some ticket packages). This world-class luau-style dinner show features incredible fire dancing, music, and storytelling. A memorable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a quick bite at a fast-food spot before heading north (~$8–$10)
meals.lunch: Included buffet lunch at the Polynesian Cultural Center (included in most ticket packages)
meals.dinner: Included in the Ha: Breath of Life dinner show package, or grab affordable food from the Center's food court (~$12–$15)

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is about 35 miles north of Waikiki — plan for a 45–60 minute drive. Book tickets online for best prices and to avoid sellouts. This is a full-day commitment and well worth it for families.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free self-guided walking tour of downtown Honolulu. Visit Iolani Palace (tours from $25/adult, $6/child) — the only royal palace on US soil. Walk to the King Kamehameha Statue and the Hawaii State Capitol. All within easy walking distance of each other.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Entry is ~$25 per adult and $17 per child. Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium, and science exhibits. Great for curious kids and adults alike.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Chinatown for an affordable and delicious dinner. Explore the vibrant night market atmosphere, street art, and local eateries. Chinatown is one of Honolulu's most colorful neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Local diner breakfast near the hotel — eggs, rice, and spam (~$8–$12)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap plate lunch from a Chinatown lunch spot or food market (~$10–$12)
meals.dinner: Authentic Asian cuisine in Chinatown — try Vietnamese pho, dim sum, or Thai food (~$10–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: TheBus is a great budget option for getting around Honolulu — single ride is $3 per adult, children under 6 free. Download the DaBus2 app for real-time schedules. Chinatown is walkable from downtown Honolulu.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the North Shore of Oahu. Visit Haleiwa town — a charming surf town with art galleries, boutiques, and the famous Matsumoto Shave Ice shop. August is still surf season so watch local surfers at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Waimea Bay Beach Park — a stunning crescent beach great for swimming in summer (waves are calmer in August). Explore the Waimea Valley botanical garden (~$20 per adult, $10 per child) and swim at the waterfall pool inside.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Honolulu and stop at a roadside shrimp truck on the North Shore (Giovanni's Shrimp Truck is iconic — ~$14 per plate). Enjoy dinner with an ocean view before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a pastry in Haleiwa town at a local cafe (~$8–$10)
meals.lunch: Shave ice from Matsumoto's (~$4–$6) and a quick snack from a local grocery or food stand
meals.dinner: Famous shrimp truck on the North Shore — garlic shrimp plate (~$14–$16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A rental car is highly recommended for North Shore exploration. The drive from Waikiki to Haleiwa is approximately 45–60 minutes. North Shore shrimp trucks are cash-preferred — bring small bills. Waimea Valley is a beautiful and educational stop for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (boat shuttle tickets are also free but must be reserved in advance at recreation.gov). Arrive early as tickets go fast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at Pearl Harbor — visit the USS Bowfin Submarine Museum (~$15 per adult, $8 per child) and walk the outdoor exhibits. The Battleship Missouri Museum is also nearby (~$29 per adult) if budget allows. Spend time at the visitor center exhibits and film.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening. Take a sunset catamaran cruise along the Waikiki coastline — budget options available from ~$35–$50 per person. Watch the sun dip below the horizon from the water — a magical family experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast sandwich or acai bowl near the hotel before heading to Pearl Harbor (~$8–$12)
meals.lunch: Pearl Harbor visitor center cafe or pack a lunch from a nearby grocery store (~$10–$12 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual beachside restaurant in Waikiki — try fresh fish and chips or a burger (~$14–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is approximately 10 miles from Waikiki — accessible by TheBus or rental car. Reserve USS Arizona Memorial boat tickets well in advance (weeks ahead if possible). The site is solemn — remind children to be respectful. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy the Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout — known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific.' Drive to Kauai or if already on Kauai, head to Waimea Canyon State Park (free entry). The canyon stretches 14 miles long and 3,600 feet deep with breathtaking red-and-green vistas. The Canyon Trail and Cliff Trail are family-friendly options.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Waimea Canyon — hike to Waipoo Falls (4-mile round trip, moderate difficulty) for a rewarding waterfall swim. Alternatively, drive to the Kalalau Lookout at Kokee State Park for dramatic Na Pali Coast views. Both are free and spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Waimea town for dinner and a stroll along the historic plantation-era main street. Visit the Captain Cook Monument and enjoy the small-town Kauai atmosphere before heading back.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from a grocery store before heading to the canyon — granola bars, fruit, and yogurt (~$6–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch at a canyon lookout — sandwiches, trail mix, and plenty of water (~$8–$10 per person)
meals.dinner: Local plate lunch or casual restaurant in Waimea town — try fresh fish or a Hawaiian plate (~$12–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Note: If your hotel is on Oahu, Waimea Canyon is on Kauai and requires an inter-island flight (~$60–$100 one-way on budget carriers like Southwest or Mokulele). Plan this as a day trip or adjust if staying on Oahu. Wear sturdy hiking shoes and bring rain gear as canyon weather can change quickly. Bring at least 2 liters of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your last morning at the hotel's beachfront — take a final swim, collect a few shells as souvenirs, and soak in the last views of the Pacific. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and begin packing. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the front desk if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Ala Moana Center (largest open-air shopping mall in the US) — budget-friendly finds at Longs Drugs, local boutiques, and the ABC Store chain. Pick up macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, Hawaiian host chocolates, and local jams as affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours early for international/mainland flights. Enjoy one last Hawaiian meal at the airport — try a plate lunch from one of the terminal restaurants as a final taste of the islands.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a splurge at a beachside cafe for a memorable last morning meal (~$12–$15)
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch at Ala Moana Food Court — wide variety of cuisines at budget prices (~$10–$14)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or grab a bento box and musubi from an airport convenience store (~$12–$15)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed. Keep some cash for tips and last-minute purchases. Take TheBus or a shared shuttle to the airport to save money on your final transfer. Double-check all travel documents, souvenirs packed safely, and enjoy the memories of your Hawaiian adventure!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Take a short stroll along the beachfront if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit / airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel's 24-hour lobby bar or room service to unwind after the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Pre-arrange airport transfer through the resort. Confirm check-in details ahead of time for a smooth late-night arrival. Hydrate well and get a good night's rest to beat jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning getting oriented – walk the beachfront, dip your toes in the ocean, and explore the resort amenities (pool, beach chairs, etc.).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beach for a relaxed afternoon of swimming and sandcastle building. Rent snorkel gear from the resort beach shack for a casual first snorkel in the calm waters near the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Hawaiian sunset from the beachfront. Enjoy a casual dinner at a nearby open-air restaurant to ease into island life.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet – enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, and fresh-squeezed juice (~$20–$30/person).
meals.lunch: Grab poke bowls from a local food truck or casual beachside café (~$15–$20/person).
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki or similar mid-range oceanfront restaurant – fresh fish tacos, grilled mahi-mahi, and tropical cocktails (~$30–$45/person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule – let the family decompress from travel. Pick up sunscreen, reef-safe products, and snacks from a nearby ABC Store or grocery.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach – Book a group family surf lesson (2 hours) at Waikiki Beach. Instructors are family-friendly and beginners are very welcome. The gentle rolling waves make this the perfect first surf experience for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, relax on Waikiki Beach. Grab shave ice from a local stand and explore the Waikiki beachfront promenade. Visit the Duke Kahanamoku statue for a classic Hawaii photo.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Waikiki's open-air shopping district (Royal Hawaiian Center or International Market Place) for souvenirs and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before surf lessons – granola, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Island Vintage Shave Ice and a plate lunch from a local deli near Waikiki (~$12–$18/person).
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon or Ramen Nakamura – affordable, delicious, and family-friendly (~$10–$15/person).

day_by_day.notes: Book surf lessons in advance as spots fill up quickly in August. Wear rash guards for sun protection. Lessons typically include board rental and instruction.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay – Reserve timed entry tickets well in advance (required). Arrive early to watch the mandatory marine education video, then spend the morning exploring one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. See sea turtles, tropical fish, and vibrant coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Hanauma Bay and spend a relaxing afternoon at the resort pool or beach. Let kids enjoy the resort's family amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet dinner near the resort to rest after an active morning.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before heading to Hanauma Bay (~$20–$30/person).
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or purchase from the snack bar at Hanauma Bay (limited options, so packing is recommended).
meals.dinner: Kona Brewing Company Hawaii or similar mid-range spot – burgers, fresh fish, and craft drinks (~$25–$35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay REQUIRES advance online reservations – book 2 days before at the latest. Entry fee is approximately $25/adult; children under 12 are free. Use only reef-safe sunscreen. Arrive early to secure the best snorkeling spots.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip – Depart early for the Polynesian Cultural Center on the North Shore of Oahu. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian villages: Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Watch canoe pageants, try traditional foods, and enjoy cultural demonstrations. The center is immersive and engaging for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular evening show – 'Ha: Breath of Life' – a world-class Polynesian performance featuring fire dancing, drumming, and traditional storytelling. Dinner package available on-site.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departing (~$15–$20/person).
meals.lunch: Island Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center – included in many ticket packages, featuring Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes (~included or ~$25/person separately).
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner or Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center – traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian cuisine (~$30–$50/person depending on package).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an all-inclusive package (Ambassador or Super Ambassador) for best value – it includes the buffet, evening show, and access to all villages. The drive from Waikiki is about 1 hour each way. Consider booking a shuttle or tour bus to avoid driving and parking hassles.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the full day at PCC. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a morning swim at the resort beach. Explore tide pools near the resort or take a gentle coastal walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby family-friendly attraction such as the Waikiki Aquarium or Diamond Head State Monument (short, rewarding hike with panoramic views – 1.6 miles round trip, suitable for families).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset beach picnic or casual dinner. Visit a local farmers' market if one is available in the area.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local bakery – try Leonard's Bakery for famous malasadas (~$10–$15/person).
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In – a beloved local institution serving plate lunches with rice, macaroni salad, and grilled meats (~$10–$15/person).
meals.dinner: Nico's Pier 38 or similar local seafood spot – fresh catch of the day, casual atmosphere (~$20–$30/person).

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head hike requires a small entry fee (~$5/person). Go early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau (if on Maui) OR book a similar authentic luau experience on Oahu such as Paradise Cove Luau. Spend the morning preparing – dress in Hawaiian attire and head to the luau venue by late afternoon for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pre-luau: Explore a local beach or shopping area. If traveling to Maui for the luau, take an early inter-island flight (book in advance). Old Lahaina Luau is considered one of the most authentic in all of Hawaii.
day_by_day.evening: Luau experience – Immerse the family in authentic Hawaiian culture with traditional hula dancing, fire knife performances, live music, and a traditional imu (underground oven) feast featuring kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort (~$15–$20/person).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near the luau venue – local plate lunch or food truck (~$12–$18/person).
meals.dinner: Included as part of the luau feast – a full traditional Hawaiian spread (~$130–$160/adult, $70–$90/child, tickets must be booked well in advance).

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau is one of the most sought-after experiences in Hawaii and sells out months in advance – BOOK IMMEDIATELY. If staying on Oahu, substitute with Paradise Cove Luau (~$100–$130/adult) which is equally family-friendly and highly rated. The luau typically begins at sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day if you did an inter-island trip, OR explore the North Shore of Oahu. Visit Haleiwa Town for local art galleries, shave ice at Matsumoto's, and the charming plantation-era architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the North Shore beaches – Sunset Beach, Ehukai Beach (Banzai Pipeline), and Waimea Bay Beach Park. In August, the waters are calm and ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Waimea Bay's famous rock jump is a family favorite.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a beach bonfire (if permitted) or resort entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Matsumoto's Shave Ice and coffee from a local café in Haleiwa (~$8–$12/person).
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck – a legendary North Shore food truck serving garlic shrimp plates (~$15–$18/person).
meals.dinner: Back near the resort – Cheesecake Factory at Royal Hawaiian Center or a mid-range local restaurant (~$25–$40/person).

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 45–60 minutes from Waikiki. Rent a car for the day for flexibility. In August, North Shore waves are small and safe for families – perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout – If visiting Kauai, take an early inter-island flight. Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon is a must-see. Start with the Waimea Canyon Lookout and Pu'u Ka Pele Lookout for stunning panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a family-friendly hike on the Canyon Trail or the Iliau Nature Loop (easy, 0.3 miles) for younger children. For more adventurous families, the Waimea Canyon Trail (3.5 miles round trip) offers incredible views into the canyon.
day_by_day.evening: Return from Waimea Canyon and enjoy a relaxed evening. If on Kauai, explore Poipu Beach for a sunset swim before returning to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure – resort or airport café (~$15–$20/person).
meals.lunch: Yumi's or Wrangler's Steakhouse in Waimea Town – local comfort food near the canyon (~$15–$25/person).
meals.dinner: The Eating House 1849 in Poipu or a similar mid-range Kauai restaurant – local fish, Hawaiian-inspired cuisine (~$30–$45/person).

day_by_day.notes: If staying on Oahu and not flying to Kauai, substitute this day with a visit to Kualoa Ranch (Jurassic Valley ATV tour or movie site tour – extremely family-friendly) or Pearl Harbor Historic Sites. Book Kauai inter-island flights and rental car well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii – wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a peaceful walk along the shoreline, collect shells, and soak in the views from the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping – pick up Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, Hawaiian sea salt, and local crafts. Pack bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant to celebrate the trip. Head to the airport for departure (confirm flight times and allow extra time for check-in).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast one final time – splurge slightly on the full buffet to fuel the travel day (~$25–$35/person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café or food court near the shopping area (~$12–$18/person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant – Roy's Hawaii Kai or Orchids at Halekulani for a memorable final meal (~$40–$60/person).

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM – arrange late checkout if possible or store luggage with the concierge. Confirm return flight details and airport transfer. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international or mainland departure.

experiences.name: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout
experiences.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails through lush valleys and dramatic red-rock formations. Kids will love spotting native birds and waterfalls along the way. The lookout points are easily accessible even for younger children.

experiences.name: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach
experiences.description: Waikiki's gentle, rolling waves make it the world's best spot to learn to surf. Group family surf lessons with certified instructors are fun, safe, and beginner-friendly. Most families are standing on their boards within the first lesson, creating unforgettable memories on one of the most iconic beaches in the world.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip
experiences.description: Spend a full day exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Families can participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional canoe rides. The evening show features a spectacular Broadway-style performance with stunning costumes and storytelling.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity and late-night room service.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: In-room late-night dining: Fresh island fruit platter, local poke bowl, and complimentary champagne welcome from the resort

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport greeter and luxury SUV transfer. Request early check-in amenities and chilled beverages in-room before arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — enjoy a sunrise stroll along the beachfront, followed by a full breakfast at the resort's signature ocean-view restaurant. Explore the resort pool and beach amenities to acclimate to island time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surfing Lessons at Waikiki Beach — head to Waikiki for a private family surf lesson with a certified instructor. Waikiki's gentle rolling waves are perfect for beginners and kids alike. Lessons include all boards and safety equipment.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Enjoy a relaxed family dinner at a premier Honolulu restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Orchids at Halekulani — renowned oceanfront brunch with fresh island fruits, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light beachside bites and fresh coconut water provided by the surf school or nearby Waikiki Beach concession
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion with fresh Hawaiian seafood; reserve a private dining booth

day_by_day.notes: Book the private family surf lesson at least 2 weeks in advance. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously. Children under 6 may prefer a shallow-water introduction session.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — depart early (7:00 AM) to secure entry before the daily cap is reached. Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. Private guided snorkel tour recommended for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Enjoy the resort's private beach with luxury cabana service, paddleboards, and kayaks. Optional: book a 60-minute family massage at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the Waikiki coastline — sip champagne, spot dolphins, and watch the sky turn gold over Diamond Head.

meals.breakfast: Early in-room breakfast from room service before departure — acai bowls, fresh pastries, and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Plumeria Beach House at Kahala Hotel — elegant open-air dining with fresh catch of the day and island salads
meals.dinner: Azure Restaurant at Royal Hawaiian Hotel — beachfront fine dining featuring Hawaiian-caught fish, prime steaks, and local farm produce

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online; book 2–3 days prior. Entry is capped daily. Bring underwater cameras or rent GoPros for memorable snorkel footage.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Day Trip — depart by 9:00 AM for the full-day experience on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian villages representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Participate in hands-on cultural activities including fire-making, canoe paddling, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the afternoon 'Rainbows of Paradise' canoe pageant on the lagoon and explore village demonstrations. Private VIP guided tour available for the family.
day_by_day.evening: HA: Breath of Life evening show at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a spectacular theatrical production featuring 100 performers, fire dancers, and live music. Dinner included with the premium package.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — buffet spread with Hawaiian staples including poi, lomi salmon, and fresh pineapple
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at Polynesian Cultural Center — included in the Ambassador VIP package with island-themed cuisine
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center — included with evening show package; traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, haupia, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Ambassador VIP package for priority seating, private guide, and all-inclusive dining. Round-trip private transportation from the resort is recommended — approximately 45 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui (approximately 30 minutes). Upon arrival, check in to a pre-arranged luxury suite or continue from Aegean Bliss if the resort spans islands. Morning helicopter tour over Maui's dramatic landscapes including Haleakalā crater, the Road to Hana waterfalls, and the West Maui Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic town of Lahaina — browse galleries, boutiques, and the famous Banyan Tree. Private guided cultural walking tour of Front Street and the old whaling district.
day_by_day.evening: Luau at Old Lahaina Luau — immerse the family in authentic Hawaiian culture with a traditional luau featuring hula dancing, fire knife performances, imu ceremony, and a lavish Hawaiian feast right on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Light grab-and-go from resort before early departure — fresh fruit, granola bars, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Mala Ocean Tavern, Lahaina — award-winning oceanfront dining with fresh island fish tacos, ceviche, and organic salads
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — all-inclusive traditional Hawaiian feast with kalua pig, poi, fresh fish, tropical cocktails, and desserts

day_by_day.notes: Old Lahaina Luau books out months in advance — reserve immediately. The luau is widely considered the most authentic on Maui. Arrive 30 minutes early for the imu (underground oven) ceremony unveiling.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakalā — depart at 3:30 AM for the summit of Haleakalā volcano (10,023 ft) to witness one of the world's most breathtaking sunrises above the clouds. Wrap in warm layers; temperature at summit is near 40°F. Private guided sunrise experience with hot beverages and breakfast provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided Road to Hana adventure — travel in a private luxury 4WD vehicle along the legendary 64-mile coastal highway. Stop at Twin Falls, Wai'anapanapa Black Sand Beach, and Oheo Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools). Picnic lunch prepared by a private chef served at a scenic waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lahaina/resort area. Relaxed family evening with resort pool time and a casual but upscale dinner.

meals.breakfast: Private catered sunrise breakfast at Haleakalā summit — hot coffee, pastries, and fresh fruit boxes
meals.lunch: Private chef picnic along Road to Hana — fresh poke, sandwiches, tropical fruit, and local snacks at a waterfall viewpoint
meals.dinner: Mama's Fish House, Paia — legendary Maui institution; reserve weeks ahead for fresh-caught fish named by the fisherman who caught it

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā National Park requires a timed entry reservation for sunrise — book exactly 60 days in advance at 7:00 AM HST on recreation.gov. Bring very warm layers for the summit. Road to Hana is a full day — start early.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Kauai — the 'Garden Isle.' Check in to luxury accommodations. Morning spent exploring the breathtaking Na Pali Coast via private boat charter — sea caves, cascading waterfalls, and spinner dolphins alongside the boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Waimea Canyon Hike and Lookout — known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific,' Waimea Canyon offers breathtaking views and family-friendly hiking trails. Visit multiple lookout points including Waimea Canyon Lookout and Pu'u Hinahina Lookout. Private naturalist guide leads the family through the canyon's geological history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a cliffside bar overlooking the Na Pali Coast. Quiet, elegant family dinner in Poipu or Princeville.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or quick resort breakfast before departure — fresh pastries and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Catered picnic lunch provided by the boat charter company — fresh island sandwiches, tropical fruit, and cold drinks enjoyed on the water
meals.dinner: The Beach House Restaurant, Poipu — iconic oceanfront dining with spectacular sunset views, fresh Hawaiian fish, and fine wines

day_by_day.notes: Na Pali Coast boat charters operate from Port Allen or Hanalei Bay — morning departures are calmer. Waimea Canyon is about 1 hour from Lihue; wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring water. Canyon trails are suitable for children 6 and older.

day_by_day.morning: Private horseback riding along Kauai's lush North Shore trails with ocean views — a magical family experience through tropical rainforest and along sea cliffs. Suitable for all ages and experience levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poipu Beach afternoon — relax at one of Kauai's most beautiful beaches, known for calm, family-friendly waters and frequent Hawaiian monk seal sightings. Enjoy luxury beach cabana service with chilled towels, fresh fruit, and cocktails. Optional glass-bottom kayak tour of the nearby sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset helicopter tour over Kauai — soar over the Na Pali Coast, Waimea Canyon, and Wailua Falls for a bird's-eye perspective of the island's stunning landscapes. Private family charter available.

meals.breakfast: Merriman's Café, Poipu — farm-to-table breakfast with local eggs, avocado toast, and Hawaiian-grown coffee
meals.lunch: Tidepools Restaurant at Grand Hyatt Kauai — romantic open-air thatched-roof huts over koi ponds; fresh island fish and salads
meals.dinner: Red Salt at Koa Kea Hotel — sophisticated modern Hawaiian cuisine with farm-fresh ingredients and an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the helicopter tour in the afternoon/evening for the best lighting over the Na Pali Coast. Helicopter tours are weather-dependent — have a flexible backup plan. Poipu Beach is consistently rated one of America's best beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Return flight to Oahu. Morning at leisure — final beach time, resort pool, or optional spa treatments at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast with no rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Diamond Head State Monument hike — a moderate 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit of Oahu's iconic volcanic crater with panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific. Family-friendly with stunning photo opportunities at the top. Private guide optional.
day_by_day.afternoon_secondary: Luxury shopping at Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's premier open-air luxury mall featuring Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co., and local Hawaiian designer boutiques. Pick up premium gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final night celebration dinner — the family's grand farewell to Hawaii. Reserve at one of Honolulu's most exclusive restaurants for a memorable last evening. Followed by a private beachfire experience at the resort with s'mores, stargazing, and Hawaiian music.

meals.breakfast: Halekulani Hotel's House Without a Key — legendary open-air oceanfront breakfast with live Hawaiian music and hula; iconic Honolulu experience
meals.lunch: MW Restaurant, Honolulu — James Beard-nominated chef Michelle Karr-Ueoka's acclaimed modern Hawaii regional cuisine
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani — Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining restaurant; Relais & Châteaux property with French-inspired tasting menu using local Hawaiian ingredients; formal attire required

day_by_day.notes: La Mer requires advance reservations and smart casual to formal dress. This is the trip's signature dining moment — consider the full tasting menu with wine pairing. The private beachfire experience should be pre-arranged with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach walk along the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort. Pack and prepare for checkout. Resort concierge arranges private luxury transfer to Honolulu International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Hawaii — private airport greeter assists with check-in and lounge access. Reflect on 10 extraordinary days of beaches, culture, and family memories.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full à la carte spread with eggs cooked to order, fresh tropical fruits, loco moco, and Kona coffee; savor every bite
meals.lunch: Airport dining at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport — Makai Market or pre-arranged premium airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or upon arrival at home destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from Aegean Bliss Resort (typically until 2:00 PM for premium guests) to maximize your final morning. Pre-purchase any duty-free items and confirm all luggage weight limits — Hawaiian souvenirs and macadamia nuts add up quickly! Arrange lei farewell ceremony with the resort for a traditional Hawaiian send-off.
